title: preview.start is an async daemon command that runs the preview and writes its receipt
description:
SPIDR child 2 of task-dd86f35e117e4de1b5b885332d8af1f8, filed by architect-aa54e231 2026-09-06. Carries task-dd86f35e's DoD item 3 (a preview can be STARTED by a production path) and the first clause of its item 7 (a new kind rotates the shared contract). dependsOn task-0e87ab34 (the shared-contract slice) and task-dd86f35e (which composes the supervisor into the daemon and owns the decide edge).

WHY A COMMAND AND NOT A LIFECYCLE HOOK - the measurement that settled the design (reproduce it before re-litigating):
(1) `moe-wrapper` and `moe-daemon` are SEPARATE bin entries in apps/daemon/package.json - separate OS processes sharing only the SQLite store.
(2) The node lander - the only writer of `outcome: "COMMITTED"` (node-lander.ts:255), reached through `createRepositoryDeliveryRuntime` - is constructed at agent-wrapper-main.ts:160 and NOWHERE else. A landing hook therefore runs in the WRAPPER.
(3) `createPreviewSupervisor` holds live previews in an in-memory Map (preview-supervisor.ts:56). A preview started in the wrapper is invisible to the daemon, so `supervisor.decide()` would find nothing to stop and daemon shutdown could not sweep it.
(4) `preview.decide` is served by the DAEMON's command plane, so the supervisor must live in the daemon.
(5) `git grep -n "setInterval" -- apps/daemon/src` returns zero production hits: the daemon has no tick loop, and an affordance READ must never spawn a product server.
Conclusion: the daemon must be told to start a preview, by a command. `runPreview` spawns a dev server and drives Playwright, so it cannot be a synchronous CommandHandler - it belongs on the ASYNC entry seam.

THE SEAM ALREADY EXISTS AND IS NAMED FOR THIS. apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-async-entries.ts holds `AsyncCommandKind` (foundation.dispatch, foundation.verification, repository.bootstrap). Its own comment says repository.bootstrap lives there rather than in the registry because the registry "is past its size cap, and this module is exactly the seam it spreads for async kinds" - daemon-command-registry.ts is 531 lines, already over the 400-line split threshold, so preview.start MUST NOT add a synchronous branch to it.

WHAT task-dd86f35e HANDS YOU (read its completionSummary and reviewSummary via get_context.epicSiblings rather than re-measuring HEAD): the preview supervisor constructed once in the daemon composition root and reachable as a port, plus the daemon shutdown path that closes it. Take that port; do NOT construct a second supervisor - two instances would each hold half the live roster and shutdown would sweep only one.

DO NOT RE-IMPLEMENT THE RUNNER. apps/daemon/src/preview/ is landed, green and correct (commit 6de79b6cb074d4a02f89b862727eb0f9c789153b, 93 tests). `createPreviewSupervisor().start(request)` already: dedupes in-flight starts by the deterministic `previewReceiptId(projectId, goalId, sha)`; records STARTED or REFUSED(code) through `recordPreviewReceipt`, which is idempotent by receipt id and answers `replayed: true` on a repeat; refuses a path-escaping goalId or sha; and never throws. This row adds the EDGE that calls it.

FENCE: preview.start is an OPERATOR act on the same terms as preview.decide - human-only (HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS, orchestrator/agent-spawn-contract.ts:229) and MCP-excluded (mcp-tool-allowlist.ts). Epic rail 4 binds: operator-only principal, MCP-excluded, every refusal carrying a stable code asserted WITH its layer.

REFUSAL VOCABULARY: mint every refusal through `previewRefusal` (preview-contracts.ts:142), which takes NO layer - `PREVIEW_CODE_LAYERS` decides. Never pass a layer literal. If start needs a code the four-code map does not name, ADD it to PREVIEW_CODE_LAYERS rather than minting a fifth spelling at a call site; `PREVIEW_CODES` is that map's key set and cannot drift.

CONTENTION WARNING (epic rail 3): daemon-command-vocabulary.ts, daemon-command-families.ts and daemon-command-payload-keys.ts are shared rosters. Never freeze a count literal in a test or a DoD - run the leg and take the PRINTED expected-vs-received as authoritative.
definitionOfDone: preview.start is on the daemon roster: daemon-command-vocabulary.ts (WiredCommandKind, its capability, OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS, and the human-act roster next to preview.decide), daemon-command-families.ts (its family flag and required capability) and daemon-command-payload-keys.ts (its exact payload key roster). Its payload decoder lives beside the decide decoder in preview-contracts.ts and refuses an inexact key set with a code minted through `previewRefusal`, never a layer literal.

preview.start is registered as an ASYNC command entry in daemon-command-async-entries.ts (NOT as a synchronous branch in daemon-command-registry.ts, which is already 531 lines and over the split threshold), and its handler calls the supervisor port composed by task-dd86f35e - it does NOT construct a second createPreviewSupervisor.

A preview STARTED through the real command writes a receipt via recordPreviewReceipt carrying {goalId, sha, url, pid, screenshots[], STARTED}, and the receipt is read back through `readPreviewReceipt` (the production read surface) rather than from the writer's return value. Assert the receipt fields, not merely that a write happened.

A start that cannot run records a REFUSED receipt carrying its code - an absent receipt and a refused one are different states and the operator's screen needs the difference. Assert the persisted receipt's code, read back through readPreviewReceipt.

Each refusal preview.start can raise is asserted with the layer PREVIEW_CODE_LAYERS names for it, over the REAL registry/async edge, with every other gate made passable so the arm pins WHICH layer answered (global rail 1). A test asserting merely that start refused is vacuous - a second refusal layer can answer first and it stays green.

The fence is bidirectional (global rail 9): preview.start is in HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS and excluded from the MCP allowlist, and the guarding test asserts BOTH directions - every advertised human-only kind is served AND every served operator kind is advertised - by enumerating the served set from the dispatch seam's handled kinds, not only from the roster constant. Assert set-equality, not a subset.

The shared contract is already rotated by task-0e87ab34 (dependsOn). Confirm at HEAD that "preview.start" is on RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS and that the digest mirrors agree BEFORE editing; if the census disagrees, that is a prerequisite regression to report, not to re-fix here. Re-run `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` and quote its count line, because this row's roster edits can still break it.

Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines, each standalone and foreground: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`. A leg printing no count line RAN NO TESTS and is not a pass (global rail 8). Repo-wide red is attributed by the merge-base-vs-HEAD path-attributed baseline (global rail 3) and disclosed verbatim.
taskRails: COMPOSE, DO NOT REBUILD. apps/daemon/src/preview/ is landed and green (commit 6de79b6c, 93 tests). Take the supervisor port task-dd86f35e composed into the daemon; never construct a second createPreviewSupervisor - two instances each hold half the live roster and shutdown sweeps only one.

ASYNC ENTRY, NOT THE REGISTRY. daemon-command-registry.ts is 531 lines, past the 400-line split threshold. daemon-command-async-entries.ts exists precisely for long-running kinds and its own comment says so. Adding a synchronous preview.start branch to the registry is a rejection.

EVERY REFUSAL THROUGH `previewRefusal`. preview-contracts.ts derives the layer from the closed PREVIEW_CODE_LAYERS map so a call site cannot mint a code/layer pair that disagrees. Never pass a layer literal. A code the map does not name is added to the MAP, not spelled at the call site.

A NEW PRODUCTION MODULE UNDER src/ NEEDS A NAME-MATCHED `<module>.test.ts` SIBLING IF IT SHIPS A `.js` BRIDGE. runtime-entrypoint.test.ts classifies a module with no name-matched sibling as TEST tier and reports its bridge as `unexpected` - this exact trap cost task-f5a74c23 a round. The expected disclosed `unexpected` array at filing time is one entry, `repository\deployment\deployment-docker-probe.js`; anything containing `preview\` is THIS row's bug.

NEVER FREEZE A ROSTER COUNT (epic rail 3). daemon-command-vocabulary.ts, -families.ts and -payload-keys.ts are contended by every concurrent kind-publishing row. Run the leg and take the PRINTED expected-vs-received as authoritative.

implementationPlan.description:
MEASURE THE PREREQUISITES AND EVERY ROSTER NUMBER. This step EDITS NOTHING. Every number below is a landmark for locating a line, never a value to type into code.

(1) PREREQUISITE GATE — both were UNMET when this was planned, so prove them before building. `git grep -n "preview.start" -- apps packages` must now show the kind on `RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS` in `packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts` (task-0e87ab34's deliverable). Read task-dd86f35e's completionSummary and reviewSummary from `get_context.epicSiblings` — NOT by re-measuring HEAD — and record the EXACT name and module path of the supervisor port it composed into the daemon. IF `preview.start` IS ABSENT FROM THE SHARED CONTRACT, or dd86f35e exposes no supervisor port, STOP and `moe.report_blocked` naming the missing symbol. Do not plan around it and do not construct a supervisor yourself (task rail 1).

(2) ONE PROBE, EVERY NUMBER AT ONCE. Write a throwaway probe that prints `Object.keys(PAYLOAD_KEYS).length`, `[...OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS]`, `[...MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS]`, `[...deps.registry.keys()]` and `PREVIEW_CODES`. Paste its FULL SOURCE and its output into the step note, then delete it. At planning time the registry size literals read 54 at five sites in `daemon-command-registry.test.ts` (:911, :956, :1809, :1831, :1863) and the exclusion rosters read 17 at three sites (`daemon-command-registry-human-approver.test.ts` twice, `mcp-main.test.ts` once, whose header also documents a `14 x 2 = 28` case total). CONCURRENT ROWS MOVE ALL OF THESE. Take the printed values as authoritative (epic rail 3).

(3) CONFIRM THE MCP EXCLUSION IS STILL DERIVED. `mcp-tool-allowlist.ts:73-83` says `MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS` is computed from `OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS` less `MCP_REACHABLE_OPERATOR_KINDS`, so this row edits that file NOT AT ALL. Read the current source and confirm. If it has been hand-kept since, it joins the owned path set — say so in the note; the plan has cap headroom for it.

(4) BASELINE THE GATES AT YOUR MERGE-BASE so a later red is attributable (global rail 3): `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`. Record each failing path with exact lines and each `Test Files N passed` count line. The daemon leg gets its own standalone foreground call at the maximum timeout.

THE CONTRACT: kind, payload roster, decoder, refusal code. All in `apps/daemon/src/preview/preview-contracts.ts` (249 lines at measurement), beside the decide decoder exactly as DoD 1 requires.

ADD `export const PREVIEW_START_COMMAND_KIND = "preview.start" as const;` beside `PREVIEW_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND` (:43).

ADD `export const PREVIEW_START_PAYLOAD_KEYS = Object.freeze(["goalId", "sha"] as const);`

**`workspace` IS DELIBERATELY NOT A PAYLOAD KEY, AND THIS IS THE SECURITY DECISION OF THE ROW.** `PreviewRunRequest` carries `{goalId, sha, workspace}`, but `preview-runner.ts:82-93` reads `<workspace>/package.json` and the runner spawns a script out of it. Accepting a caller-supplied workspace would be arbitrary command execution on the daemon host for anyone who can reach the command plane. The handler resolves workspace from the daemon's own bound configuration in step 5. Write that reason in a comment on the key roster so a later reader cannot "helpfully" add the third key.

ADD `decodePreviewStartPayload(value: unknown)` modelled on `decodePreviewDecidePayload` (:225). EXACT ARITY: own enumerable keys are exactly the two named, both non-empty strings within `MAX_PREVIEW_TEXT`. A missing key and an unknown key both refuse. Bound both, and reject any `goalId` or `sha` containing a path separator, `..`, a NUL or a non-NFC form — the receipt id and the capture path are derived from them (`previewReceiptId`), and the supervisor's own escape check is a second gate, not a reason to skip the first.

ADD ONE CODE TO THE MAP, NOT AT A CALL SITE: `PREVIEW_START_PAYLOAD_INVALID: "REQUEST"` in `PREVIEW_CODE_LAYERS` (:82-92). `REQUEST` is already in the closed `PREVIEW_LAYERS` (:72), so this mints no new layer literal. `PREVIEW_CODES` derives from the map's keys and needs no edit. Mint every refusal through `previewRefusal(code)` (:142), which takes NO layer (task rail 3). Reuse the four existing codes wherever they fit rather than adding more.

Report the file's new `wc -l`. It will pass the 250 target and stay far under the 400 split threshold; do NOT split it in this row — it is contended by concurrent preview rows.

THE VOCABULARY ROSTERS — three files, all coupled, landed together so HEAD is never half-registered.

`apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.ts` (371 lines), FOUR sites, each located by its `preview.decide` neighbour:
  - `PREVIEW_FAMILY` (:160-161) is a single-key record `Readonly<Record<typeof PREVIEW_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND, string>>` mapped to `CAPABILITIES.REVIEW`. Widen the type and add the start kind. Capability: `REVIEW`, matching its twin — start and decide are two halves of one operator act.
  - `WiredCommandKind` (:203-213) — add `| typeof PREVIEW_START_COMMAND_KIND`.
  - the agent-mapping branch at :250 (`if (kind === PREVIEW_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND) return null`) — a human act maps to NO agent; widen it to cover both.
  - `OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS` (:324-343) — add the kind. THIS ONE EDIT IS WHAT FENCES THE COMMAND: `mcp-tool-allowlist.ts:73` derives the MCP exclusion from this set, so membership here removes the kind from the advertised MCP surface with no edit in that file.

`apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-families.ts` (195 lines), :113 — `preview: kind === PREVIEW_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND` is an EQUALITY, not a set membership. It must widen to admit both kinds. This compiles either way and reds only in the family arm, so it is easy to miss (risk H).

`apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-payload-keys.ts` (179 lines) — add `[PREVIEW_START_COMMAND_KIND]: PREVIEW_START_PAYLOAD_KEYS` beside the decide entry. NOTE THE ORDERING CONSEQUENCE: `REGISTRATION_ORDER` in `daemon-command-registry.test.ts` is transcribed and follows `PAYLOAD_KEYS` DECLARATION ORDER, not alphabetical and not the async-entries record order. Where you place this line decides what step 6 must transcribe.

HEAD IS RED AFTER THIS STEP AND THAT IS EXPECTED — the kind is declared but not yet served, which reds the set- and order-equality arms at `daemon-command-registry.test.ts:912` and `:957`. Step 5 closes it. Do not green the tree here by editing those arms; step 6 owns them.

THE HUMAN-ONLY FENCE. `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawn-contract.ts` (250 lines) — add `preview.start` to `HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS` beside `preview.decide` (:229).

WHAT THIS ACTUALLY BUYS, so the arm in step 7 tests the right thing: `HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS` is consumed by `agent-wrapper.ts:353`, which makes the wrapper REFUSE TO STAFF the kind — an agent offered `preview.start` as READY skips it instead of claiming it. That is a behavioural property, not a roster fact, and it is asserted against the wrapper, not by reading the constant back.

CONFIRM, DO NOT EDIT, THE MCP SIDE. `mcp-tool-allowlist.ts` gets NO edit this row: `MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS` (:73-83) is derived from `OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS`, which step 3 already extended, and `WIRED_KINDS` (:87-93) filters `Object.keys(PAYLOAD_KEYS)` through that exclusion. Re-read both after step 3 and record in the step note that the advertised surface dropped the kind WITHOUT a hand edit. If it did not, the derivation has been broken by a peer — that is a stop-and-report, not a hand edit here.

THE TWO FENCES ARE DIFFERENT AND BOTH ARE REQUIRED. `OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS` fences the COMMAND PLANE (only the configured operator principal may send it). `HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS` fences the WRAPPER (no agent may staff it). Epic rail 4 wants both; neither implies the other.

THE ASYNC ENTRY AND ITS HANDLER — the step that makes the kind SERVED and greens the equality arms step 3 reddened.

NEW MODULE `apps/daemon/src/preview/preview-start-command.ts`, modelled on `repository/repository-bootstrap-command.ts` (220 lines), the async-entry precedent. It exports `createPreviewStartHandler(options): AsyncCommandHandler`. PLUS its `.js` bridge (`export * from "./preview-start-command.ts";`) AND, mandatorily, the name-matched `preview-start-command.test.ts` sibling in step 7 — without it `runtime-entrypoint.test.ts` classifies the module TEST tier and reports the bridge as `unexpected` (task rail 4; this trap cost task-f5a74c23 a round).

WHAT THE HANDLER DOES, in order:
  1. FENCE AT ENTRY, before the clock and before any effect, exactly as `repository-bootstrap-command.ts:190-193` does: `principal.principalId !== options.operatorPrincipalId` -> throw `DomainRefusal("OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED", "DAEMON_AUTHORIZATION", ..., 403)`. THE ASYNC ENTRY MUST FENCE ITSELF — the registry's operator check lives in the SYNCHRONOUS handler path, which an async entry never reaches, so `OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS` membership alone would leave the kind dispatchable by any ADMIN-capable session. That was measured on the bootstrap row; do not rediscover it.
  2. Decode with `decodePreviewStartPayload`; on refusal throw the refusal minted by `previewRefusal`, carrying the layer `PREVIEW_CODE_LAYERS` assigns.
  3. RESOLVE `workspace` FROM DAEMON CONFIGURATION, never from the payload (step 2's reason). An unconfigured workspace refuses with a code from the map — it does not default and it does not guess.
  4. Call `options.supervisor.start({goalId, sha, workspace})` — THE PORT COMPOSED BY task-dd86f35e, taken as an option. NEVER call `createPreviewSupervisor` here (task rail 1): two instances each hold half the live roster and shutdown sweeps only one, leaking a dev server holding a port.
  5. READ THE RECEIPT BACK with `readPreviewReceipt(store, projectId, previewReceiptId(projectId, goalId, sha))` and answer from THAT. **Do not call `recordPreviewReceipt`** — `preview-runner.ts:126` already recorded it, on both the STARTED and REFUSED paths. A second write would be silently absorbed by the ledger's idempotence and answer `replayed: true`, looking correct while hiding a double-write (risk D).
  6. `supervisor.start` never throws and returns `PreviewRunResult`; on `ok: false` the receipt is already REFUSED with its code, so answer the refusal with that code and its mapped layer rather than inventing one.

REGISTER IT in `apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-async-entries.ts` (130 lines): add the kind to the `AsyncCommandKind` union (:30-37) with a comment saying WHY it is async — `runPreview` spawns a dev server and drives Playwright, which a synchronous `CommandHandler` cannot express, and `daemon-command-registry.ts` is 531 lines and past its split threshold (task rail 2). Add the supervisor port to `AsyncCommandEntryOptions`, and add the entry to the returned record in the shape the bootstrap entry uses (:110-116): `{asyncHandler, handler: foundationSyncHandler, kind, payloadKeys: PAYLOAD_KEYS[PREVIEW_START_COMMAND_KIND], requiredCapability}`. Use the SPREAD idiom already in that file for optional members — under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` an explicit `undefined` differs from an absent key.

THE ROSTER CONSUMER BACKFILL — six transcribed test files that red the moment steps 3-5 land. Mechanical, but every one is a HAND transcription that exists to be the independent side of a comparison. DO NOT REPLACE ANY OF THEM WITH A DERIVED EXPRESSION: a list computed from the roster under test asserts that the roster equals itself. Edit each by hand and move its literal.

1. `daemon-command-registry.test.ts` — the heaviest. `ROWS` (transcribed, each with capability/agent/code/layer/payloadKeys — add the start row), `REGISTRATION_ORDER` (:327, transcribed, order follows `PAYLOAD_KEYS` DECLARATION order, so insert at the slot step 3 chose, NOT alphabetically), `OPERATOR_ONLY`, and the size literals at :911, :956, :1809, :1831, :1863. The set-equality arm at :912 and the order arm at :957 are DERIVED and green themselves once the transcriptions are right.
2. `daemon-command-registry-human-approver.test.ts` — `expectedExclusions` (a transcribed list) plus TWO `toHaveLength(17)` literals that must move together.
3. `mcp-main.test.ts` — `EXPECTED_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS` (transcribed) and the `kinds x entries` total its header documents as `14 x 2 = 28`. Both move.
4. `daemon-command-vocabulary.test.ts` — its transcribed kind roster and family/capability row.
5. `daemon-store-dependencies.test.ts` — `registryKinds` in the plain-Node smoke child, a transcribed SET whose own comment says "A new command writes its own kind here". The set-equality arm at :238 is DERIVED and needs nothing.
6. `daemon-v2-command-registry.test.ts` — a single `ports.registry.size` literal.

TAKE EVERY NUMBER FROM THE PRINTED EXPECTED-VS-RECEIVED, NEVER FROM ARITHMETIC AND NEVER FROM THIS PLAN. At measurement the registry read 54 and the exclusions 17; concurrent kind-publishing rows move both hourly (epic rail 3, task rail 5). Run the leg, read the diff it prints, write that.

`mcp-http/mcp-http-host.test.ts` is DERIVED — it reds until the exclusion roster above is right, then greens with no edit. Do not edit it.

THE BEHAVIOURAL ARMS — the row's real evidence, in three files.

**`apps/daemon/src/preview/preview-start-command.test.ts` (NEW — also discharges the name-matched-sibling requirement of task rail 4).** Drive the REAL registry/async edge with an injected supervisor port and a real store; never call the handler function in isolation for the receipt arms.
  (A) DoD 3 — A STARTED PREVIEW WRITES ITS RECEIPT. Start through the real command, then read the receipt back with `readPreviewReceipt` (the production read surface) and assert the FIELDS: `goalId`, `sha`, `url`, `pid`, `screenshots[]`, `STARTED`. Assert the values, not that a write happened, and read them back through the ledger rather than from the handler's return value.
  (B) DoD 4 — A REFUSED START WRITES A REFUSED RECEIPT CARRYING ITS CODE. An absent receipt and a refused one are different operator-visible states. Assert the persisted receipt's code, again read back through `readPreviewReceipt`.
  (C) DoD 5 — ONE ARM PER REFUSAL, EACH PINNING WHICH LAYER ANSWERED. For each code `preview.start` can raise, make EVERY OTHER GATE PASSABLE so the arm proves this layer answered and not an earlier one, and assert the code together with the layer `PREVIEW_CODE_LAYERS` maps it to. An arm asserting merely "it refused" is vacuous — a second refusal layer answering first keeps it green (global rail 1). Cover at minimum: the operator fence (`OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED` @ `DAEMON_AUTHORIZATION`, 403) with a non-operator ADMIN-capable session — the arm that proves the async entry fences ITSELF rather than relying on the registry's synchronous check; the decoder's `PREVIEW_START_PAYLOAD_INVALID` @ `REQUEST`; and the runner-side codes the supervisor surfaces.
  (D) NO SECOND SUPERVISOR, NO SECOND RECEIPT. Assert the handler calls the INJECTED port (spy on it) and that exactly ONE ledger row exists for the receipt id after a start — a second `recordPreviewReceipt` would be absorbed by idempotence and is invisible to a naive read.
  (E) `workspace` IS NOT ACCEPTED FROM THE PAYLOAD. Send `{goalId, sha, workspace}` and assert it refuses on exact arity, with the code and layer. This arm stops the security decision being quietly undone later.

**`apps/daemon/src/preview/preview-contracts.test.ts`** — decoder arms for `decodePreviewStartPayload`: exact arity, missing key, unknown key, empty string, over-`MAX_PREVIEW_TEXT`, and the traversal-shaped `goalId`/`sha` rejections. Assert the code and its mapped layer, never a bare null.

**`apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-planning-offers.test.ts`** — DoD 6, THE BIDIRECTIONAL FENCE. Add `preview.start` to the explicit human-only roster beside `preview.decide`. Then make the arm bidirectional as global rail 9 demands: enumerate the SERVED set from the dispatch seam's handled kinds (`[...deps.registry.keys()]`), not from the roster constant, and assert SET-EQUALITY between "served and operator-only" and "advertised human-only" — not a subset. Keep the existing explicit-roster arm too: derived-only would make the assertion `set.has(x) for x in set`, which that file's own comment (:441-444) calls out as a tautology.

MUTATION DRILL — prove the arms bind. An arm never seen red is a claim, not a test.

BEFORE MUTATING: `git status --porcelain` the exact paths and RECORD the output. `preview-start-command.ts`, its `.js` bridge and `preview-start-command.test.ts` are UNTRACKED (`??`), and `git diff` on an untracked path is EMPTY BEFORE, DURING AND AFTER a mutation — it certifies nothing, and an unrestored mutation would ride into the commit wearing a clean diff with the arms green because the mutation is what they were re-graded against (global rail 13). Back each untracked path up out of tree (%TEMP%, suffixed with your worker id).

SIX MUTATIONS, each applied ALONE, the named arm confirmed RED, then restored:
1. `preview-start-command.ts` — delete the operator fence at handler entry. Arm (C)'s `OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_REQUIRED` case reds. THE MOST IMPORTANT DRILL IN THE ROW: it is the only proof the async entry fences itself rather than inheriting a synchronous check it never reaches.
2. `preview-start-command.ts` — answer from the handler's return value instead of `readPreviewReceipt`. Arms (A) and (B) red.
3. `preview-contracts.ts` — relax the decoder to "pick the keys I know" instead of exact arity. Arm (E) reds (a `workspace` key would be silently accepted).
4. `daemon-command-vocabulary.ts` — remove the kind from `OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS`. The MCP exclusion arms in `mcp-main.test.ts` and `daemon-command-registry-human-approver.test.ts` red — also the proof that the exclusion really is DERIVED and not hand-kept.
5. `orchestrator/agent-spawn-contract.ts` — remove the kind from `HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS`. The bidirectional fence arm in `affordance-planning-offers.test.ts` reds. Confirm the SET-EQUALITY arm reds and not merely the explicit-roster arm — if only the hand-named roster catches it, the bidirectional half is not doing its job and must be fixed before proceeding.
6. `daemon-command-families.ts:113` — revert the widened equality to the decide-only form. The family arm reds. This is the edit that compiles either way (risk H), so it is worth confirming something watches it.

AFTER RESTORING, prove restoration in a tool call SEPARATE from the restore. TRACKED paths: `git diff -- <path>` empty. UNTRACKED paths: SHA256 equality against the out-of-tree backup, computed and compared explicitly — a PowerShell copy can silently no-op and "the command returned" is not evidence the bytes moved. Record every hash pair.

GATES AND ADVERSARIAL REVIEW. Load the `adversarial-self-review` skill and read your own diff as an attacker first.

THREE GATES, each standalone and foreground, never piped and never `;`-chained (a pipe reports tail's exit code; a chain reports only the last command's). Quote each `Test Files N passed` COUNT LINE — an exit-0 leg with no count line RAN NOTHING and calling it a pass is a false completion claim (global rail 8):
  1. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` — the long one, measured at 560-2006s on this board; its own call at the maximum timeout.
  2. `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` — DoD 7 requires it even though this row edits no control-room file, because the roster edits can still break it.
  3. `pnpm typecheck`.

1. **Roster row, then async-entry row — REJECTED, measured.** `daemon-command-registry.test.ts:912` asserts `[...deps.registry.keys()].sort()` EQUALS `ROWS.map(row => row.kind).sort()`, and `:957` asserts `[...deps.registry.keys()]` EQUALS the transcribed `REGISTRATION_ORDER` **in order**. **THIS IS A RECURRING POLICY GAP, NOT A ONE-OFF.** The `repository.bootstrap` row is the same shape and landed as a **sixteen-path completion commit** — the worker met the consumers one at a time. That is precisely the mid-flight discovery global rail 19 now forbids at plan time. Every future daemon command kind will hit this same wall: the roster transcriptions are deliberate anti-vacuity design (a derived expectation would assert the roster equals itself), so they red atomically, and one new kind is structurally a ~17-file change.

**DECISION NEEDED (any one unblocks it):**
- raise the live daemon's `maxAffectedFiles` for roster-backfill rows, or
- grant this row an explicit size exception, or

**Two design decisions already settled, so they are not re-litigated later:**
- `workspace` is **not** a payload key. `preview-runner.ts:82-93` reads `<workspace>/package.json` and spawns a script from it, so a caller-supplied workspace is arbitrary code execution on the daemon host. `PREVIEW_START_PAYLOAD_KEYS` is exactly `["goalId","sha"]`; workspace resolves daemon-side.

MEASURED AT HEAD (moe/work-2026-09-04). `preview.decide` is the exact twin of the kind this row adds, so its consumer set is ground truth: `git grep -l "preview\.decide" -- apps/daemon/src packages` returns TWENTY files. THE RUNNER ALREADY WRITES THE RECEIPT — the edge must NOT. `preview-runner.ts:126` calls `recordPreviewReceipt(config.store, {...})`. `supervisor.start()` returns `PreviewRunResult` and records NOTHING itself (preview-supervisor.ts:99-129 holds no ledger call). So the description's claim that start "records STARTED or REFUSED through recordPreviewReceipt" is TRUE, but via `runPreview`, one layer down. The handler therefore calls `supervisor.start()` and READS BACK through `readPreviewReceipt`; it must never record a second receipt.

2. THE RUNNER CONTRACT. `PreviewRunRequest` = `{goalId, sha, workspace}` (preview-runner.ts:64-70). `PreviewRunResult` = `{ok:true, started:{handle, receipt}}` | `{ok:false, receipt: PreviewReceiptV1|null, refusal}` (:77-79). `PreviewRunnerConfig` (:52-62) carries `projectId` and `store`.

3. `workspace` IS A COMMAND-EXECUTION SURFACE. `workspaceScripts` (preview-runner.ts:82-93) reads `<workspace>/package.json` and the runner spawns a script out of it. See risks — the payload roster is `["goalId","sha"]` and workspace resolves daemon-side.

Four codes exist: PREVIEW_COMMAND_MISSING/RUNNER, PREVIEW_DECISION_INVALID/REQUEST, PREVIEW_GOAL_NOT_LANDED/GOAL_AUTHORITY, PREVIEW_START_TIMEOUT/RUNNER. `PREVIEW_LAYERS` (:72) is the closed layer set: GOAL_AUTHORITY, REQUEST, RUNNER.

THE SECURITY DECISION OF THIS ROW, AND IT IS NOT NEGOTIABLE: `workspace` IS NOT A PAYLOAD KEY. `PreviewRunRequest` carries `{goalId, sha, workspace}`, but `preview-runner.ts:82-93` reads `<workspace>/package.json` and spawns a script out of it. So `preview-start-command.ts` needs BOTH `preview-start-command.js` AND `preview-start-command.test.ts`.
